FPM_FSE_receive and avg_err_show.0.  Each entry is a wrong reading of the
disassembly that t_fpm_fse_recv claims to kill, and a good many of them are
the readings V22_FSE_receive would have suggested -- the point of the set is
that the two blocks are cousins and not copies.
TWO SURVIVORS, and both are recorded rather than left as holes.
`the RE-rotation's upper fold is exclusive` moves the re-rotation angle by
exactly 0x8000 at a half-angle of 0x4000 and at no other input.  The suite
DOES land on that half-angle -- t_fpm_fse_recv counts the sweep positions
that reach it and fails if none does, which is what separates this from an
untested claim -- and nothing it compares moves.
THAT LAST CLAUSE USED TO READ `because FPM_phasor reduces 0x8000 and 0 to
the same table index, the same fraction and the same quadrant`, AND THE
QUADRANT PART OF IT WAS WRONG.  A phase of 0x8000 is read as a signed short,
so the quadrant is -4 and not 0, and the sign lookups land four entries
before each table (D392, finding 3588).  The equivalence survives that, but
as two separate coincidences rather than one identity: the index is 0 and
the fraction is 0 either way, so the cosine takes the sign at index -4, which
IS FPM_sin_sign[0] in the object and is 16384, the same as FPM_cos_sign[0];
and the sine takes the sign at index -4, which is COEF_DC[2] in the object
and is 28620 rather than 16384 -- a different multiplier that changes nothing
because sin_table[0] is zero.  BOTH READINGS ARE NOW MEASURED: D392 is closed
on both halves, the two windows are values in fpm_phasor.c rather than
whatever the link puts below each table, and t_fpm_phasor sweeps sine and
cosine over the whole 16-bit range (finding 3700).  Note
that the sibling entry, `the re-rotation does not lift a
negative angle`, IS caught: it shifts the angle over a whole quarter of the
input range rather than at one point, and lands where the two sides' phasor
arguments differ in ways the reduction does not absorb.
`a short tail is stashed on a zero count too` widens `left > 0` to
`left >= 0` inside a loop whose own condition is `left != 0`, so the value
it admits cannot occur.  The live reading of that test is covered by
`a one-sample tail is dropped rather than stashed` instead.
